newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar suggests Israel invite linked to peace talks.
newsitem.headline: Qatar suggests Israel invite linked to peace talks.

text.p: Qatar suggested on Sunday that its invitation for Israel to attend the Middle East-North Africa (MENA) economic summit in November would depend on resumption of Arab-Israeli peace talks.
"There is a long time between now and November and a lot of things can happen...It is our hope in Qatar that peace talks do resume," said Fawaj al-Attiyah, spokesman at Qatar's foreign ministry.
Attiyah was briefing reporters at the end of a two-day visit by Syrian Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara to Qatar.

"There are still a few months before the conference in November. The actual stage in which Qatar will be issuing invitations is still not nigh," Attiyah said. "Coordination and consultations continue between the U.S. and the State of Qatar and other Arab countries and Qatar in regard to the peace process."
He added: "It is our feeling in Qatar that Israel's policy of settlement does not at all in any way encourage the peace process and talks to resume."

Israeli-Palestinian peacemaking was plunged into deep crisis in March when Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu began a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem and a Moslem militant bomber killed himself and three Israeli women in Tel Aviv.
Attiyah said on Saturday it expected Israel to attend the conference, saying it was a purely economic forum.
Doha is hosting the conference, the fourth since landmark peace negotiations began in 1991. Israel attended all three previous summits.

Qatar and Oman had established trade links with Israel after the Jewish state signed a peace deal with the Palestinians in 1993. But they both said they had frozen ties with Israel following what they consider hardline policies by Netanyahu.
Attiyah said al-Shara's visit "was part of continued coordination and consultation between the two countries".
